title: Luong et al. (2011): Multiple Choice
instructions: Choose the answer that best reflects the review's mechanisms, research designs, and limits.

items.prompt: Which account best captures the review's explanation of more positive relationships in later life?
options: Larger networks alone account for higher satisfaction among all older adults
Personal regulation, social circumstances, and partners' responses work together
Partners' kindness determines relationship quality independently of older adults' own behavior
Improved physical functioning directly explains satisfaction without any role for social goals
items.answer: Personal regulation, social circumstances, and partners' responses work together
items.explanation: The review integrates motivation, appraisal, social expertise, conflict management, roles, and reciprocal social input. It does not identify a single exclusive cause or promise the same outcome for every individual.

items.prompt: According to SST, which shift in priorities follows a more limited perceived time horizon?
options: Prioritizing distant information gains while reducing the value of emotional meaning
Maintaining every peripheral and close relationship with exactly equal investment
Abandoning all social goals and withdrawing from every relationship
Giving present relationship satisfaction greater priority than future information gains
items.answer: Giving present relationship satisfaction greater priority than future information gains
items.explanation: Expansive time favors knowledge and contacts useful for the future. As perceived time shortens, present-oriented emotional goals receive greater priority.

items.prompt: How does the review interpret smaller social networks in later life?
options: Proactive reduction of peripheral ties helps preserve meaningful close relationships
Every reduction follows the death of a partner and therefore reflects only involuntary loss
Close support disappears in exactly the same proportion as peripheral social contacts
A smaller network necessarily produces better emotional outcomes in every circumstance
items.answer: Proactive reduction of peripheral ties helps preserve meaningful close relationships
items.explanation: The authors emphasize active restructuring of networks and relative preservation of intimate ties. This account does not deny bereavement or the problems of having too few close partners.

items.prompt: What is a defensible interpretation of the positivity-bias evidence reviewed?
options: Older adults experience no actual interpersonal conflict
Older adults' appraisals are invariably more accurate than independent observations
Attention and appraisal can make older adults' accounts of difficult relationships more positive
The reviewed studies found the identical attentional bias in younger and older adults
items.answer: Attention and appraisal can make older adults' accounts of difficult relationships more positive
items.explanation: Older spouses evaluated interactions more positively than observers, and older participants focused less on hypothetical negative comments. These findings concern appraisal and attention; they do not establish the absence of conflict.

items.prompt: Why did Hess and colleagues interpret their impression-updating findings as evidence of social expertise?
options: Older adults responded selectively to stable traits harmful to relationships
Older adults rejected all new information, whether it described one act or a stable pattern
Younger adults were uniquely able to recognize repeated dishonesty in potential partners
Participants were randomly assigned to experience the breakdown of a real long-term relationship
items.answer: Older adults responded selectively to stable traits harmful to relationships
items.explanation: Older adults updated impressions in response to trait-diagnostic information such as repeated dishonesty, rather than any contradictory act. Similar judgments among socially active younger adults suggest a contribution from social experience.

items.prompt: Which combination matches the findings on arguments and avoidance?
options: Only older adults reacted emotionally during arguments; avoidance equalized the age groups
Older adults were consistently less reactive during both arguments and avoided arguments
Younger adults alone showed reduced reactivity in every type of conflict situation
Argument reactivity was similar; avoidance brought reduced reactivity only for older adults
items.answer: Argument reactivity was similar; avoidance brought reduced reactivity only for older adults
items.explanation: When younger and older adults argued, their increases in distress were similar. When both used the same avoidance strategy, only older adults reported reduced reactivity. This conditional benefit does not establish avoidance as the best response to every problem.

items.prompt: Which example illustrates how changing roles may reduce interpersonal stress?
options: All family and marital conflicts disappear biologically at a particular chronological age
Retirement and an empty nest can reduce demands and increase choice of partners
Older adults cease all family contact regardless of culture, housing, or health
Caregiving and bereavement automatically improve every older adult's relationship satisfaction
items.answer: Retirement and an empty nest can reduce demands and increase choice of partners
items.explanation: Leaving work and full-time childcare may remove difficult demands. The review also discusses substantial distress from spousal caregiving and bereavement, so favorable role changes are not universal.

items.prompt: What reciprocal process is proposed by the Social Input Model (SIM)?
options: Network size increases automatically without any changes in social behavior
Biological changes in one person alone produce all improvements in relationships
Older adults' positive regulation and partners' kind responses reinforce each other
Younger generations withdraw completely from relationships with older people
items.answer: Older adults' positive regulation and partners' kind responses reinforce each other
items.explanation: SIM describes dynamic influence between partners. Older adults may cultivate positive interactions, while others reciprocate through kindness, reduced blame, forgiveness, and efforts to avoid conflict.

items.prompt: What happened when a vignette kept the social transgression constant but changed the offender's age?
options: Respondents predicted stronger confrontation and public blame only for the older offender
Offender age made no difference to the responses participants expected
Respondents predicted disengagement only when the offender was younger
Respondents predicted more avoidance toward older offenders and more direct responses toward younger ones
items.answer: Respondents predicted more avoidance toward older offenders and more direct responses toward younger ones
items.explanation: Participants reported what they thought the offended character would do. The age-varying vignette supports differential treatment, but does not show that the treatment necessarily arose from respect.

items.prompt: What response may follow the perception that little time remains in a relationship?
options: Greater priority for harmony, avoidance of arguments, and forgiveness
More confrontation solely to maximize information for a distant shared future
Immediate termination of every relationship regardless of the problem or partner
The complete disappearance of any connection between time perspective and forgiveness
items.answer: Greater priority for harmony, avoidance of arguments, and forgiveness
items.explanation: Imagined constraints on contact and the reviewed forgiveness studies support a possible role for relationship time horizons. The authors retain conditional language, and avoidance without forgiveness can leave resentment unresolved.

items.prompt: How can a negative age stereotype produce more favorable treatment in the studies reviewed?
options: It proves that the stereotype accurately describes every older person's abilities
It establishes that older adults cannot intentionally commit a social transgression
Attributing conduct to forgetfulness can reduce perceived intent, blame, and punishment
It leaves judgments of intent and responsibility unchanged but eliminates every age difference
items.answer: Attributing conduct to forgetfulness can reduce perceived intent, blame, and punishment
items.explanation: In the ambiguous unpaid-hat vignette, older women were more often judged forgetful and punished less. Kinder treatment can arise from a negative assumption; it does not validate the stereotype or establish uniformly respectful attitudes.

items.prompt: What explained Japanese older adults' greater reported difficulties with grown children in the cross-cultural study?
options: Every Japanese participant was 96 years old
Differences in living with adult children
The universal superiority of larger American social networks
Different conventions for selecting holiday greeting cards
items.answer: Differences in living with adult children
items.explanation: The study included Japanese and U.S. participants aged 13 to 96. The difference in problems with grown children was explained by co-residence, highlighting household arrangements as part of the cultural context.

items.prompt: Which finding shows a possible limit to the benefits of a small close network?
options: Having fewer than three close partners was linked to loneliness and lower satisfaction
Each lost partner invariably caused a clinical disorder in every older adult
The number of close partners had no relationship with unmet social needs
Larger networks reduced satisfaction by the same amount at every adult age
items.answer: Having fewer than three close partners was linked to loneliness and lower satisfaction
items.explanation: Older adults reporting fewer than three close partners also reported less social embeddedness, more loneliness, and lower satisfaction. This study finding distinguishes selective closeness from unmet social needs; it is not a universal numerical requirement.
items.source: When a network becomes too small

items.prompt: Which alternative explanation do the authors explicitly retain for sentimental-card findings?
options: No previous study has ever measured older adults' satisfaction with social relationships
Earlier generations' card-giving norms may produce a cohort effect
All reviewed studies used one identical sample without cultural or relationship variation
The number of social partners cannot be measured by any research method
items.answer: Earlier generations' card-giving norms may produce a cohort effect
items.explanation: More sentimental cards for older recipients may reflect generational norms. The authors call for studies distinguishing cohort explanations from mechanisms proposed by SIM.

items.prompt: Which conclusion respects the review's proposed research agenda?
options: Aging guarantees the same improvement in relationships for every individual
The reviewed mechanisms establish direct improvements in physical health and functioning
Relationships may improve, with limits related to cohort, network adequacy, and circumstances
Self-reported age differences establish the causal effect of aging on relationship quality
items.answer: Relationships may improve, with limits related to cohort, network adequacy, and circumstances
items.explanation: The authors call for attention to overly small networks, greater freedom over schedules, and illness-related social control by spouses, as well as cohort alternatives. These conditions may facilitate or undermine relationship quality.
